question: An international treaty, designed to protect human health and phase out the use of mercury, was signed in 2013 at ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Minamata, Japan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Minamata Convention on Mercury is an international treaty designed to protect human health and the environment from anthropogenic emissions and releases of mercury and mercury compounds.
 
• This treaty was signed in 2013 in Minamata, Japan, a city that experienced severe mercury poisoning in the mid-20th century, leading to the naming of the convention.
 
• The convention aims to phase out the use of mercury in various products and processes, control emissions, and regulate mercury mining and trade.
 
• It includes provisions for the safe storage and disposal of mercury waste, as well as measures to reduce mercury pollution in artisanal and small-scale gold mining.
 
• The treaty entered into force on August 16, 2017, after ratification by over 50 countries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Mercury is a toxic element that poses significant risks to human health and the environment. It can cause neurological and behavioral disorders, particularly in developing fetuses and young children.
 
• The Minamata Convention is named after the Japanese city of Minamata, where industrial discharge of mercury into the water caused widespread mercury poisoning, known as Minamata disease, in the 1950s and 1960s.
 
• The convention was developed under the auspices of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and is part of global efforts to address environmental pollution and promote sustainable development.
 
• Countries that are parties to the convention are required to develop national action plans to reduce mercury emissions and releases, promote the use of alternatives, and raise public awareness about the risks of mercury exposure.
 
• Implementation of the Minamata Convention is supported by the Global Environment Facility (GEF) and other international organizations, which provide technical and financial assistance to countries in their efforts to comply with the treaty's provisions.
